subject: physics
question_text: The error in the measurement of the radius of a sphere is 1%. What is the error in the measurement of its volume?

verification.note: Unit 2 has NO Short Answer or Long Answer section in EITHER source book — the Fastrack (pp.4-5) and the TSBIE Basic Learning Material (pp.2-3) both list Very Short Answer questions only. So every Unit 2 card is a 2-mark VSAQ and no 8-mark form is invented. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The relation used
lines: Volume of a sphere V = (4/3) π r³
so V ∝ r³. For a power law the percentage
steps.why: A quantity raised to a power multiplies its percentage error by that power, because the relative changes add once for each factor of r.
common_mistakes: Using the surface area formula, which gives a factor 2 instead of 3.

recall.must_convey: That volume is proportional to r cubed, so the percentage error is three times the percentage error in r.

steps.memory_tip: The power becomes the multiplier: r³ makes the error 3 times bigger.
steps.margin_note: Write V = (4/3)πr³ first. The 3 comes from there.

steps.label: The answer
steps.why: The constant (4/3)π has no error of its own, so it does not enter the percentage error at all.
common_mistakes: Writing 1% because the constant was thought to matter.
Cubing the 1% to get 1%, instead of multiplying by 3.

recall.must_convey: That the error in the volume is three percent.

steps.memory_tip: Multiply by the power, never raise to it: 3 × 1% = 3%.

insider_note: The power 3 becomes the multiplier 3. Write the volume formula first — it is where the 3 comes from.
